source.title: Winterreise, D. 911 — No. 24 Der Leiermann (later version)
source.edition: OpenScore Lieder transcription from IMSLP #60822; printed-edition imprint not independently established

voices.name: Voice (baritone; treble notation sounds one octave lower)

bars.description: Printed bars 1–61 once, all five poem stanzas written out in the later-version A-minor source. The first performed bar includes 0.0546875 quarter units of common MIDI pre-roll for the source's initial grace note, then its full three metric quarters; subsequent bars remain exactly three quarters. No strophic or hurdy-gurdy refrain repeat is inserted.

endpoints.basis: Windows selected from absolute-pitch inspection of the cached Commons transfer. The final window isolates the last written piano attack, not the later surface-noise cutoff; see work/schubert-winterreise-leiermann-preparation-end.png. No listening annotation is claimed.

provenance: OpenScore Lieder releases these encodings under CC0: https://github.com/OpenScore/Lieder#license-and-acknowledgement . Exact downloaded MXL bytes match the inventory SHA-256. This is voice and piano, not an orchestral arrangement; Mutopia 373 is Einsamkeit and is not used.

Source part P1 is Singstimme (one treble-clef vocal line); P2 is Pianoforte (two staves with explicitly numbered MusicXML voices). Each source voice is mapped to a distinct MIDI track in one simultaneous compilation, not independently re-timed or inferred from register. The engraving retains the original vocal staff, two piano staves and all lyrics. These are encoding identities, not source-separated audio or MIDI-patch-derived instruments.

The recording is Hans Duhan, baritone, with Ferdinand Foll, piano (1928): Christian Utz, ZGMTH 18/Sonderausgabe (2021), https://www.gmth.de/zeitschrift/artikel/1132.aspx . The conventional treble vocal line sounds one octave below its written pitches. The engraving labels that octave convention explicitly; no vocal lyrics are stripped.

Transposition describes the sounding pitches of this particular Commons transfer relative to the global librosa tuning estimate, not a claim about the historical performers’ selected key or original tuning. Utz footnote 73 explicitly warns that Duhan’s transferred pitch/key is particularly uncertain. Absolute piano spectra, not filenames or a global key-classifier label, determine the configured shifts.

Opening piano A2/E3 drone becomes nominal G2/D3: measured peaks 100.1/150.4 Hz (4.0–4.5 s), at global tuning +44 cents (A=451.326 Hz). Additional global shift −2 semitones; vocal line an additional −12. This pitch match is measured; the filename’s later-version label alone is not evidence of recorded pitch.

The source begins with a real piano-lower-5 grace note. Isolated compilation introduced a 0.0546875-quarter startup lead only in that voice; simultaneous named-voice compilation gives every voice the same origin. Preserve the initial grace and account for the common lead in performed bar 1 rather than dropping a note, moving individual regular attacks, or drifting the parts independently.

        \new Staff
